pathway.title: Legence Corp. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Revenue durability is the weakest dimension because growth is concentrated in data-centre construction. Data centers and technology supplied 62.6% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 39.2% a year earlier and 86.26% of the revenue increase, while all other end markets together grew 22.39%. New building is now 61.1% of revenue, the vast majority of contracts are fixed-price, and the bulk of performance comes late in a project, so a client deferral cuts revenue and raises working-capital needs at once. Maintenance & Service, the most recurring line, fell to 10.03% of revenue from 13.28% a year earlier, so little of the base repeats under contract. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C51

Contracted visibility equals about two thirds of a year's revenue but is partly bought. Backlog is 77.24% higher than a year ago, and 65% to 75% of it is expected to convert within 12 months, which equals 61.41% to 70.86% of last-twelve-month revenue. The issuer attributes part of the increase to the Bowers acquisition, and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio, which excludes acquired additions, slipped to 1.2x from 1.5x. That is still above 1.0x, so organic awards remain ahead of revenue by a narrowing margin, and a ratio below 1.0x would signal falling revenue. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 73–75; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C47; calculation C6; calculation C7

Adjusted margins are holding through a mix shift, but the reported cushion is thin. Adjusted EBITDA margin is 12.5% against 11.7% a year earlier, yet nine-month gross margin fell to 18.89% from 21.43% because the lower-margin Installation & Maintenance segment rose to 84.14% of revenue from 69.46%, while that segment's own margin rose to 16.58% from 15.67% and Engineering & Consulting fell to 31.13% from 34.51% on higher compensation, a shift toward project management and lower design margins. Reported EBITDA is 6.99% of last-twelve-month revenue against 12.34% on the issuer's adjusted basis, and because fixed-price contracts and wages are the largest costs, overruns land directly on creditors' cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C16; calculation C17

Cash conversion is good but flattered by timing. Free cash flow after capital expenditure for the last twelve months equals 98.18% of reported EBITDA and 55.59% of adjusted EBITDA, yet FY2025 included a working-capital inflow while the nine months of 2026 absorbed an outflow, cash taxes paid rose 147.62%, and the issuer expects capital expenditure to increase for fabrication capacity. Conversion therefore depends on customer advances and supplier credit continuing as revenue scales, and a slowdown would reverse both. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124–125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C27

Liquidity covers identified near-term calls about three times, and the only maintenance covenant is not live. Cash plus the USD 169.3 million undrawn revolver covers the USD 90.0 million cash price of the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01, deferred consideration, current debt and the current tax receivable payment 3.02x, or 1.60x if the whole USD 150.0 million buyback authorisation were also used. The springing 8.50x first lien net leverage test applies only when revolver usage passes USD 70.0 million and letters of credit already use USD 30.7 million of that, so the test is not live. Net debt over adjusted EBITDA of 1.28x is only an orientation, because the covenant uses the executed definition of consolidated pro forma adjusted EBITDA, which the filings describe only in summary, so covenant headroom is not calculated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C34

Leverage is moderate, but financial policy has turned from repayment to growth and returns, and the sponsor's pledged stake adds control risk. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01) after the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, but the group has since drawn a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, completed three acquisitions and authorised a USD 150.0 million buyback. The credit agreement also lets the borrower add pari passu debt, subject to conditions, while first lien net leverage is no greater than 5.25x and, by management's estimate at 2025-12-31, about USD 1.4 billion of junior secured and USD 1.5 billion of unsecured debt, so the current ratio does not bind financial policy. Blackstone-linked holders owned about 61% of the votes in March 2026 and an indicative 46.67% in November 2026 on share-count arithmetic, they have pledged all their shares, and the tax receivable agreement and sponsor-linked lenders align cash and votes with the sponsor rather than with creditors. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

Refinancing risk is low before 2030, but interest-rate protection rolls over within weeks and the margin depends on ratings. The revolver matures on 2030-09-22 and the term loan on 2031-12-16, while swaps covering 79.27% of the term loan expire on 2026-12-31 and forward swaps cover 60.59% from that date, so 39.41% floats unhedged above a 0.75% SOFR floor. The June 2026 rating upgrades by two agencies triggered a further cut of 0.25 percentage points in the term loan margin, which depends on ratings being maintained, and the rating levels themselves are not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C36; calculation C37; calculation C38

runs.text: The four main supports are liquidity and maturities, cash generation, falling funding cost and contracted visibility; the five main constraints are data-centre concentration, acquisition-led financial policy, the quality of reported earnings, dependence on working-capital float and sponsor-linked claims on cash.

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. The undrawn USD 200.0 million revolver (USD 169.3 million available after letters of credit) and cash cover identified near-term calls 3.02x, no debt falls due before the revolver matures on 2030-09-22 apart from USD 10.0 million of yearly term loan amortisation, small acquisition notes and finance leases, and the only maintenance covenant is untested, so a liquidity-driven default over the next 12 to 24 months is unlikely. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C30

Cash generation supports debt service. Free cash flow after capital expenditure over the last twelve months equals 98.18% of reported EBITDA, and reported EBITDA covers cash interest 5.28x, so debt service does not depend on refinancing; the caveat is that FY2025 conversion included a working-capital inflow and the interest figure is net of swap settlements. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C21; calculation C23

Funding cost and leverage are falling. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), and the term loan margin moved from SOFR plus 2.25% to SOFR plus 1.75% after the May 2026 amendment and the June 2026 upgrades, which lowers the interest burden and widens refinancing options. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66

Contracted visibility and client relationships limit near-term revenue risk. Backlog is 77.24% higher than a year ago, 65% to 75% of it converts within 12 months, the ten largest clients have a 23-year average relationship and no client exceeds 10% of revenue, so next year's revenue is largely contracted although the backlog is partly acquired. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; calculation C47; calculation C6; calculation C7

Concentration in data-centre construction is the main constraint. Data centers and technology supplied 62.6% of nine-month revenue and 86.26% of its increase, clients may reduce or terminate contracts at any time, and utility or water shortages can make data-centre clients defer projects, so a pause in that capital cycle would cut revenue and margins together and shorten the backlog's life. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C3

Acquisition-led financial policy is the second constraint. Goodwill and intangibles are 41.28% of total assets, two impairments in the second quarter of 2026 followed a drop in demand for sustainability services at one Engineering & Consulting unit, and the group has drawn a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, completed three acquisitions and authorised a USD 150.0 million buyback, so acquired earnings and integration now carry leverage that reported ratios only partly capture. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C40; calculation C41

The quality of reported earnings is thin. Reported EBITDA is 6.99% of last-twelve-month revenue against 12.34% on the adjusted basis, share-based and other non-cash compensation explains over half of the gap, and management reports material weaknesses in information-technology access and journal-entry review that were unremediated at 2026-09-30, so lenders rely on figures that carry a higher chance of error. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16; calculation C17

Dependence on working-capital float is the fourth constraint. Contract assets are 97.47% higher and receivables 44.08% higher than at the year end, funded in part by payables up 78.84% and contract liabilities up 42.00%, and surety bonds outstanding rose 139.77% to USD 1,346.3 million, so a slowdown would drain cash through the same lines that now supply it and could tighten bonding capacity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C42; calculation C43; calculation C39

Sponsor-linked claims on cash are the fifth constraint. The tax receivable liability rose 65.21% since the year end and requires payment of 85% of net cash tax savings, sponsor-linked lenders hold 8.81% of long-term debt, and the sponsor's remaining stake of an indicative 46.67% of votes is pledged under margin loans; the agreement ends early on a change of control as it defines one, which includes certain mergers, asset sales and board-composition changes, and then requires a termination payment whose amount is not stated, so cash can leave for the sponsor and a forced sale could change control. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The initial public offering completed on 2025-09-15 and converted the sponsor-owned borrower into a listed holding company with an Up-C structure; net proceeds of USD 780.2 million and cash on hand prepaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, and the term loan margin fell by 0.25 percentage points. On 2025-10-30 the credit agreement was amended to extend the term loan maturity to 2031-12-16 and to replace the USD 90.0 million revolver with a USD 200.0 million revolver maturing 2030-09-22. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 173; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174

In 2026 the group used new debt and stock to buy Bowers, Metrix and then CTI: Bowers closed on 2026-01-02 with total consideration of USD 426.68 million and was partly financed by a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, Metrix closed on 2026-03-01, and CTI closed on 2026-11-01 for estimated consideration of USD 90.0 million cash and 256,411 Class A shares. The term loan was repriced on 2026-05-27 to a margin 0.25 percentage points lower, with a further 0.25 percentage points after ratings upgrades. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26

The sponsor vehicles sold stock in secondary offerings on 2025-12-16 and 2026-04-09 without proceeds to the company, and on 2026-11-10 the board authorised a USD 150.0 million share repurchase programme with no termination date. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30, first through IPO debt repayment and then through earnings growth that includes acquired businesses, shifting creditor risk to integration and cash conversion.

fields.value: The issuer states only adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived here, and the choice matters: net leverage is 2.27x on reported EBITDA (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01) but 1.28x on the issuer's adjusted figure, and share-based and other non-cash compensation explains over half of the gap. Cash interest cover improved to 5.28x on the last twelve months from 1.61x for FY2025, but cash interest is measured net of swap settlements.

fields.value: Deleveraging through FY2025 came from repaying debt, not from earnings: net leverage on reported EBITDA fell to 3.83x from 8.79x while reported EBITDA itself fell by 10.03%, because IPO proceeds and cash on hand repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan in September 2025. Adjusted EBITDA rose by 30.14% in the same year, but 72.25% of the rise in add-backs is the larger share-based compensation charge of the IPO year, so the two measures tell different stories.

fields.value: Net debt has risen again since the year end because of acquisitions, but last-twelve-month reported EBITDA has nearly doubled, so net leverage still fell to 2.27x, or 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01. Acquisition spending was the largest use of cash in the nine months, ahead of capital expenditure, so the improvement depends on the acquired businesses holding their earnings and on integration going to plan.

fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: transactions, business and revenue mix, ownership and control, governance, sponsor and shareholder behaviour, operating model and history, from the supplied filings and the source readiness findings. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legence is a Blackstone-backed building-services group growing quickly through acquisitions and data-centre work, so creditors gain scale and a larger order book but rely on a sponsor-influenced board, unremediated reporting-control weaknesses and the execution of new acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Blackstone-associated holders owned about 61% of the voting stock in March 2026 and have since sold shares, so their present control is not established, and they have pledged their holdings under margin loans. The IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan after a debt-funded distribution to the sponsor in 2024, but a new USD 150.0 million buyback authorisation and the pace of acquisitions show capital allocation moving from deleveraging to growth and returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is concentrating in one end market and in project work: data centers and technology supplied 42.7% of 2025 revenue and 62.6% of the nine months of 2026, and new building work rose to 61.1% of nine-month revenue from about 40% in 2025. The Maintenance & Service line, the closest to recurring revenue, fell from 12.95% to 10.03% of revenue, so earnings now depend more on the timing of large projects in one sector.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_lgn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The order book supports near-term revenue but is partly bought and its momentum is easing: backlog rose 77.24% year on year, the filing attributes the rise in backlog and awarded contracts to the Bowers acquisition as well as new awards, and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio slipped to 1.2x from 1.5x while staying above 1.0x. A pipeline that depends on acquired work and on one end market's capital programmes leaves cash flow less visible than the headline backlog suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor control is loosening, but the sponsor's remaining stake is pledged and its present percentage is not stated. The sponsor vehicles held about 61% of voting shares on 2026-03-24, and share counts imply 46.67% on 2026-11-09 after the April 2026 secondary offering, assuming no other transfers, which is below the 50% level at which the charter lets Blackstone nominate a majority of directors. Lower ownership weakens the sponsor's incentive to support the company and raises the chance of further sell-downs, and both vehicles have pledged all their shares and units under margin loans, so a sponsor-level default could force a sale of the controlling block.

fields.value: Cash leaves the group toward the sponsor through the tax receivable agreement and through sponsor-linked debt: the liability rose 65.21% since the year end to reflect the April 2026 exchanges, it requires payment of 85% of net cash tax savings, and sponsor-associated lenders hold 8.81% of long-term debt. These flows compete with debt service for cash and mean that amendments and voting under the credit agreement involve parties aligned with the sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sponsor's behaviour is mixed rather than extractive: it took a USD 301.6 million distribution in 2024 funded by a USD 315.0 million incremental term loan, which absorbed 95.75% of that loan, but the 2025 IPO then repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, and the sponsor's sell-downs are secondary sales that take no cash out of the company. We assign a Medium sponsor and governance risk level, driven by the 2024 distribution and the pledge of shares, with the IPO deleveraging and a board of five independent directors out of six as counterweights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting controls remain a live governance weakness: management and the auditor identified material weaknesses in information-technology access controls and journal-entry review, still unremediated at 2026-09-30, and an auditor attestation on internal control is first required for the 2026 annual report. Until remediated, covenant certificates and the reported earnings that feed them carry more risk of error than a normally controlled issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is deleveraging and diversification of ownership: the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, five of six directors are independent, the sponsor is selling rather than adding to its stake, and backlog and awarded contracts rose 92.49% year on year. The view would improve if the material weaknesses are remediated and attested for 2026, if book-to-bill returns to 1.5x, and if the new buyback is funded from cash flow rather than borrowing. It would worsen if the sponsor sells down further and the credit agreement treats a change of control as a default, or if acquisitions continue to be paid for with the term loan.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Legence Corp. (lgn-2052568), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: business and revenue durability, margins, cash conversion, liquidity, leverage tolerance, refinancing, financial policy, a qualitative downside path and monitoring triggers, from the supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance findings. No rating, security recommendation or covenant conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legence's fundamental credit profile is adequate and improving, with moderate leverage and covered near-term cash needs, but it rests on one cyclical end market and on acquired growth, so creditors bear the risk of a data-centre construction slowdown.

fields.value: Net leverage is 2.27x on reported earnings, or 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01, and cash plus the undrawn revolver covers identified near-term calls 3.02x. Data centers supplied 86.26% of the nine-month revenue increase, while the new buyback authorisation and the pace of acquisitions show financial policy moving from repayment toward growth and shareholder returns.

fields.value: Revenue durability is the weakest dimension because growth is concentrated in data-centre construction. Data centers and technology supplied 62.6% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 39.2% a year earlier and 86.26% of the revenue increase, while all other end markets together grew 22.39%. New building is now 61.1% of revenue, the vast majority of contracts are fixed-price, and the bulk of performance comes late in a project, so a client deferral cuts revenue and raises working-capital needs at once. Maintenance & Service, the most recurring line, fell to 10.03% of revenue from 13.28% a year earlier, so little of the base repeats under contract.

fields.value: Contracted visibility equals about two thirds of a year's revenue but is partly bought. Backlog is 77.24% higher than a year ago, and 65% to 75% of it is expected to convert within 12 months, which equals 61.41% to 70.86% of last-twelve-month revenue. The issuer attributes part of the increase to the Bowers acquisition, and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio, which excludes acquired additions, slipped to 1.2x from 1.5x. That is still above 1.0x, so organic awards remain ahead of revenue by a narrowing margin, and a ratio below 1.0x would signal falling revenue.

fields.value: Adjusted margins are holding through a mix shift, but the reported cushion is thin. Reported EBITDA is 6.99% of last-twelve-month revenue against 12.34% on the issuer's adjusted basis, and because fixed-price contracts and wages are the largest costs, overruns land directly on creditors' cash flow.

fields.value: Leverage is moderate, but financial policy has turned from repayment to growth and returns, and the sponsor's pledged stake adds control risk. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01) after the IPO repaid USD 780.3 million of term loan, but the group has since drawn a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, completed three acquisitions and authorised a USD 150.0 million buyback. The credit agreement also lets the borrower add pari passu debt, subject to conditions, while first lien net leverage is no greater than 5.25x and, by management's estimate at 2025-12-31, about USD 1.4 billion of junior secured and USD 1.5 billion of unsecured debt, so the current ratio does not bind financial policy. Blackstone-linked holders owned about 61% of the votes in March 2026 and an indicative 46.67% in November 2026 on share-count arithmetic, they have pledged all their shares, and the tax receivable agreement and sponsor-linked lenders align cash and votes with the sponsor rather than with creditors.

fields.value: Refinancing risk is low before 2030, but interest-rate protection rolls over within weeks and the margin depends on ratings. The revolver matures on 2030-09-22 and the term loan on 2031-12-16, while swaps covering 79.27% of the term loan expire on 2026-12-31 and forward swaps cover 60.59% from that date, so 39.41% floats unhedged above a 0.75% SOFR floor. The June 2026 rating upgrades by two agencies triggered a further cut of 0.25 percentage points in the term loan margin, which depends on ratings being maintained, and the rating levels themselves are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious view is that deleveraging and cash generation are reported, not forecast: net leverage fell to 2.27x (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), last-twelve-month free cash flow was 98.18% of reported EBITDA, two agencies upgraded the company in June 2026, and the average relationship with the ten largest clients is 23 years with no client above 10% of revenue. Those facts lower single-name risk and make a quick liquidity squeeze unlikely. The view would improve if book-to-bill stays above 1.0x while the data-centre share stops rising, if working-capital float persists without acquired help, if the control weaknesses are remediated, and if the buyback is paid from free cash flow. It would worsen if revolver usage passed USD 70.0 million, if book-to-bill fell below 1.0x, if the sponsor's margin lenders forced a sale of its controlling block, or if reported net leverage rose back toward 3.83x.

fields.value: The four main supports are liquidity and maturities, cash generation, falling funding cost and contracted visibility; the five main constraints are data-centre concentration, acquisition-led financial policy, the quality of reported earnings, dependence on working-capital float and sponsor-linked claims on cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are the main support. The undrawn USD 200.0 million revolver (USD 169.3 million available after letters of credit) and cash cover identified near-term calls 3.02x, no debt falls due before the revolver matures on 2030-09-22 apart from USD 10.0 million of yearly term loan amortisation, small acquisition notes and finance leases, and the only maintenance covenant is untested, so a liquidity-driven default over the next 12 to 24 months is unlikely.

fields.value: Funding cost and leverage are falling. Net leverage fell from 8.79x at FY2024 to 2.27x at 2026-09-30 (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), and the term loan margin moved from SOFR plus 2.25% to SOFR plus 1.75% after the May 2026 amendment and the June 2026 upgrades, which lowers the interest burden and widens refinancing options.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contracted visibility and client relationships limit near-term revenue risk. Backlog is 77.24% higher than a year ago, 65% to 75% of it converts within 12 months, the ten largest clients have a 23-year average relationship and no client exceeds 10% of revenue, so next year's revenue is largely contracted although the backlog is partly acquired.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration in data-centre construction is the main constraint. Data centers and technology supplied 62.6% of nine-month revenue and 86.26% of its increase, clients may reduce or terminate contracts at any time, and utility or water shortages can make data-centre clients defer projects, so a pause in that capital cycle would cut revenue and margins together and shorten the backlog's life.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition-led financial policy is the second constraint. Goodwill and intangibles are 41.28% of total assets, two impairments in the second quarter of 2026 followed a drop in demand for sustainability services at one Engineering & Consulting unit, and the group has drawn a USD 200.0 million incremental term loan, completed three acquisitions and authorised a USD 150.0 million buyback, so acquired earnings and integration now carry leverage that reported ratios only partly capture.

fields.value: The quality of reported earnings is thin. Reported EBITDA is 6.99% of last-twelve-month revenue against 12.34% on the adjusted basis, share-based and other non-cash compensation explains over half of the gap, and management reports material weaknesses in information-technology access and journal-entry review that were unremediated at 2026-09-30, so lenders rely on figures that carry a higher chance of error.

fields.value: Dependence on working-capital float is the fourth constraint. Contract assets are 97.47% higher and receivables 44.08% higher than at the year end, funded in part by payables up 78.84% and contract liabilities up 42.00%, and surety bonds outstanding rose 139.77% to USD 1,346.3 million, so a slowdown would drain cash through the same lines that now supply it and could tighten bonding capacity.

fields.value: Sponsor-linked claims on cash are the fifth constraint. The tax receivable liability rose 65.21% since the year end and requires payment of 85% of net cash tax savings, sponsor-linked lenders hold 8.81% of long-term debt, and the sponsor's remaining stake of an indicative 46.67% of votes is pledged under margin loans; the agreement ends early on a change of control as it defines one, which includes certain mergers, asset sales and board-composition changes, and then requires a termination payment whose amount is not stated, so cash can leave for the sponsor and a forced sale could change control.

fields.value: Legence designs, installs and maintains heating, cooling, electrical and plumbing systems for mission-critical buildings such as data centers, laboratories, hospitals and universities. It reports two segments, Engineering & Consulting at 15.86% of nine-month 2026 revenue and Installation & Maintenance at 84.14%, and most jobs other than maintenance finish within nine months. Acquisitions have changed the business in 2026: the Bowers acquisition alone explains about one third of the rise in Installation & Maintenance gross profit.

The mission-critical nature of the buildings supports client retention and bonding access, but revenue follows client capital budgets, so debt service rests on project execution and billing timing, not on a contracted annuity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legence Corp. is a listed holding company that consolidates Legence Holdings LLC, the borrower under the credit agreement, in an Up-C structure; the term loan and revolver are secured by a lien on substantially all assets of the borrower and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, and guarantors are not named. Blackstone-linked vehicles held about 61% of the votes in March 2026 and an indicative 46.67% in November 2026, which is below the 50% level at which Blackstone may nominate a majority of the board, and they have pledged all their shares and units under margin loans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors this means the sponsor's influence is declining but not gone, a forced sale by its lenders could change control, and the tax receivable agreement and related-party lenders give the sponsor claims on cash beside the credit agreement. The 2024 distribution of USD 301.6 million, funded by a USD 315.0 million term loan, shows the sponsor has extracted value before, while the IPO repayment of USD 780.3 million and sell-downs without company proceeds show support since; Business & governance rates the sponsor and governance risk as Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transactional, cyclical and concentrated, not recurring. Volume follows client capital programmes, led by data centers and technology (62.6% of nine-month revenue), with new building at 61.1%, and the issuer says downturns bring greater price competition and lower revenue and profit. Pricing power is limited on fixed-price work, where scope changes are billed but base prices are fixed, although tariffs on internationally procured materials are passed to clients and the issuer says it typically takes no exposure to equipment price increases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue outside data centers grew 22.39% over nine months, which shows demand in other markets, yet Engineering & Design revenue fell 4.66% and one Engineering & Consulting unit lost new contracts in the second quarter of 2026 as demand for sustainability services fell, and the issuer wrote down goodwill and long-lived assets there. Switching costs and long relationships (23 years on average for the ten largest clients) support retention, yet contracts can be reduced or terminated at any time, so revenue visibility depends on the backlog rather than on contract terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under a sharp project slowdown. Wages are the largest cost and the workforce is partly unionised under 44 collective agreements, so labour is semi-fixed. Subcontractor and equipment spending, 40.32% of FY2025 revenue, may be passed to clients as a line item or priced into the job, and the issuer says it typically takes no exposure to equipment price increases, which protects margin against input inflation. Because contracts are fixed-price, errors in labour estimates fall on the company, and the issuer says engineering, project management and maintenance earn higher margins than installation, the line that grew fastest at 162.76% over nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating leverage works both ways: nine-month gross margin of 18.89% against 21.43% a year earlier fell with mix, while the Installation & Maintenance margin rose to 16.58%, so resilience rests on installation project margins holding. The reported EBITDA margin of 6.99% is the conservative base, while the adjusted margin of 12.34% adds back non-cash compensation, impairments and deal costs, so conclusions on resilience should use the reported margin and treat the adjusted one as an upper bound.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is asset-light but capital expenditure is rising: purchases of property and equipment rose 143.32% over nine months and the issuer expects further increases for fabrication capacity in Installation & Maintenance. Free cash flow of the last twelve months equals 98.18% of reported EBITDA, but FY2025 free cash flow before the working-capital lines was lower than reported, while the nine months of 2026 absorbed a working-capital outflow and cash taxes paid rose 147.62%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA therefore translates into debt-service cash now, but the translation depends on customer advances and payables, which the nine-month contract liability movement shows can shrink quickly. Capital expenditure is a flexible lever in a slowdown, whereas interest, term loan amortisation of USD 10.0 million a year, operating lease liabilities of USD 163,555 thousand and the tax receivable payments are not, and the deferred consideration due on 2026-12-31 is payable in cash or shares at the company's option.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure add to fixed charges: operating leases, the tax receivable liability, surety bonds of USD 1,346.3 million and customer guarantees of USD 283.6 million, and multiemployer pension plans, to which the group contributed about USD 75.6 million in FY2025 and whose withdrawal liability the issuer says it cannot estimate. Management says it has not incurred material losses on the guarantees, so these claims matter mainly if a slowdown coincides with project losses or a union withdrawal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate to high: the issuer competes with national groups such as Comfort Systems USA and Southland Industries and with many small owner-operated firms, and price competition rises in downturns. The issuer says its integrated service offer is an advantage over smaller competitors, but the filings describe no barrier to entry beyond engineering skill, bonding relationships and client ties of 23 years on average, and small owner-operated firms already compete locally, so installation margins are exposed in a slowdown. Substitutes are not evidenced in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high on large projects because contracts are fixed-price, work is often subcontracted through general contractors and architects, and clients can reduce or terminate contracts at any time, offset by long relationships and no client above 10% of revenue. Supplier power is low for equipment and materials, which come from many vendors, with tariffs and equipment costs passed to clients, but high for scarce skilled labour, where shortages could raise wages and third-party costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three outside factors change the credit view. Interest rates and the construction cycle drive client capital budgets and the cost of the floating-rate term loan, so rate moves reach cash flow through both the hedge expiry on 2026-12-31 and client demand. Trade policy and tariffs raise material costs and delay supply; the issuer says tariffs on internationally procured materials are passed to clients, which protects margins but can slow projects. Technology investment in data centers, and the availability of water or other utility services at their sites, set the pace of the largest end market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: cash plus undrawn revolver cover identified near-term calls 3.02x; net leverage of 2.27x reported (2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01); backlog up 77.24% with 65% to 75% converting within 12 months; no client above 10% of revenue; the term loan and revolver mature in 2031 and 2030.

fields.value: - Weaknesses: data centers supply 62.6% of revenue; reported EBITDA margin of 6.99% against 12.34% adjusted; unremediated control weaknesses; sponsor-linked claims on cash; no rating levels or covenant headroom measure available.

fields.value: - Opportunities that could improve credit quality: remediation and a first auditor attestation of internal control for 2026; use of cash for repayment rather than the USD 150.0 million buyback; further backlog from data-centre and life-science clients converting without acquired help.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats that could weaken credit quality: a pause in data-centre construction; revolver usage above USD 70.0 million that activates the 8.50x test; a sponsor margin-loan default forcing a sale of the controlling block; swap expiry and a rise in SOFR; fixed-price overruns on large projects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is adequate and improving. The main supports are moderate leverage (2.27x reported, 2.56x pro forma for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01), cash generation of 98.18% of reported EBITDA, and covered near-term calls. The main constraints are revenue concentration, thin reported earnings (a 6.99% margin), acquisition-driven leverage and sponsor-linked claims. The trend is better on leverage and interest cover, which rose to 5.28x on reported EBITDA, and worse on concentration, which rose from 39.2% to 62.6% in a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C21; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Missing datapoints that would move the profile are the executed credit agreement and its definition of consolidated pro forma adjusted EBITDA, the rating levels, revenue by client or project, the earnings and net debt of acquired businesses including the one completed on 2026-11-01, and any management guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is supportive for revenue and cautious for cash. Backlog conversion, the Bowers business and the margin step-down support revenue and interest cost, while the swap expiry on 2026-12-31, the deferred consideration due on that date, capital expenditure for fabrication capacity and a cash price of USD 90.0 million for the acquisition completed on 2026-11-01 absorb cash, and a first auditor attestation on internal control is due for 2026. Book-to-bill of 1.2x says awards are still ahead of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outlook depends on how long data-centre and life-science construction stays strong, because that decides how much of the installed work turns into repeat maintenance revenue, and on how sponsor ownership evolves before the 2030 revolver and 2031 term loan maturities. No management guidance or sector forecast is supplied, so this horizon is not established beyond the issuer's own risk statements. Sector tailwinds are technology investment and building-efficiency demand; headwinds are utility constraints at data-centre sites, tariffs, skilled labour shortages and higher rates. Company tailwinds are backlog, bonding access and acquisition integration; company headwinds are the sponsor's pledged stake, the tax receivable agreement and the shift of policy toward the buyback.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with data-centre clients deferring projects, for example because utility services such as water are unavailable at a site or because a client's own capital budget is cut. The first operational break is slower backlog conversion on fixed-price new-building work, where most performance comes late in a project, with the labour force and fabrication capacity already in place; book-to-bill falling below 1.0x would confirm it. Revenue and installation margins fall together, and because wages are the largest cost and many employees are unionised, costs adjust slowly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash then falls faster than EBITDA because the float reverses: contract liabilities and payables, which grew 42.00% and 78.84% since the year end, would shrink while contract assets, up 97.47%, take longer to bill, and surety bonds of USD 1,346.3 million and letters of credit of USD 30.7 million tie up bonding capacity and revolver availability. Liquidity absorbs this: cash plus the undrawn revolver covers identified calls 3.02x, capital expenditure and the USD 150.0 million buyback are discretionary, and deferred consideration can be paid in shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the slower channel. Reported EBITDA would have to fall 33.07% before pro forma net leverage of 2.56x returned to the 3.83x of FY2025, and the springing test applies only if revolver usage passes USD 70.0 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate slowdown. A change of control would add a further call, because the tax receivable agreement ends early on one and requires a termination payment whose amount is not stated. A severe, prolonged freeze combined with a sponsor margin-loan default, a loss of the rating-linked margin step-down and weak integration of acquired businesses would be needed to threaten debt service, and the observable triggers are book-to-bill below 1.0x, revolver usage rising, negative working-capital cash flow and a sponsor sale.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lgn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C35; calculation C33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Legence presents an adequate business profile supported by backlog, long client relationships and bonding access, but credit quality is constrained by data-centre concentration, acquisition-led growth, thin reported earnings and sponsor-linked claims on cash. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow was 98.18% of reported EBITDA, though it depends on working-capital float. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the data-centre cycle, the ratings that underpin the margin step-down and the covenant staying untested; no large debt maturity falls due before 2030. The primary downside path is a pause in data-centre construction that reverses working-capital float while acquisition and sponsor claims keep cash leaving. Against typical leveraged building-services issuers the profile cannot be ranked because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the rating levels, revenue by client, and the earnings and net debt of acquired businesses. Top risk: concentration in one end market funded in part by acquisitions.
